parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the faces between which the Hall voltage $V_{\text{H}}$ is developed.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: The current $I$ is produced by charge carriers, each of charge $+q$ moving at speed $v$ in the direction of the current. The number density of the charge carriers is $n$.
parts.text: Derive an expression relating the Hall voltage $V_{\text{H}}$ to $v$, $B$ and $d$, where $d$ is one of the dimensions of the slice.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Use your answer in (b)(i) and an expression for the current $I$ in the slice to derive the expression

$$V_{\text{H}} = \frac{BI}{ntq}.$$

Explain your working.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Suggest why the Hall voltage is difficult to detect in a thin slice of copper.

stem:
A thin slice of conducting material is placed normal to a uniform magnetic field of flux density $B$, as shown in Fig. 8.1.

{{figure:figure_8_1.png}}

The magnetic field is normal to face CDEF and to face PQRS.

A current $I$ passes through the slice and is normal to the faces CDQP and FERS.

A potential difference, the Hall voltage $V_{\text{H}}$, is developed across the slice.
